checks.location: Appendix C.2, Eq18–19 (p20), and Appendix E.1–E.2, Eq31–35 (pp25–26): mutual-information surrogate and beta-weighted variational reconstruction.
checks.claim: Equations (9)/(18) assert an MI lower bound without entropy offsets, and Eq. (33) prints a beta-weighted ELBO inequality without a beta restriction.
checks.explanation: Differential entropy need not be nonnegative. Separately, decreasing a positive KL penalty below its unit ELBO coefficient can raise the objective above the log evidence.
checks.demonstration: Fix the discrete molecular graph \(X\), and let the continuous representation \(Y\) be uniform on a region of volume \(e^{-2}\). Then \(I(X;Y)=0\), \(h(Y\mid X)=-2\), and \(H(X\mid Y)=0\), so the printed entropy-free lower bound is \(1\). For the ELBO, take \(Z\sim N(0,1)\), \(Y\mid Z\sim N(Z,1)\), observe \(y=0\), and use the exact posterior \(q=N(0,1/2)\). Its KL divergence from the prior is \((\log2-1/2)/2>0\). The unit-weight ELBO equals \(\log p(0)\approx-1.265512\); choosing \(\beta=1/2\) raises it by half that positive KL divergence to approximately \(-1.217225\), contradicting the asserted bound.
checks.repair: Retain the marginal entropy offset: \[I(X;Y)=\tfrac12\{H(X)+h(Y)-H(X\mid Y)-h(Y\mid X)\},\] when the mixed discrete/continuous quantities exist. The omitted offset is harmless for optimization only when it is fixed, and does not justify the displayed inequality without a lower bound on it. Use unit KL weight for the standard ELBO; \(\beta\ge1\) also gives a lower bound because it subtracts an additional nonnegative term. For \(0\le\beta<1\), call the expression a surrogate unless the posterior KL gap compensates for the reduction. The authors’ later MoleculeSDE Appendix F keeps the entropy constants in Equation (65), uses unit KL weight in Equation (68), and introduces \(\beta\) in the proxy objective (69).
checks.scope: The entropy objection concerns the continuous formulation, not a finite empirical discrete distribution. No claim is made that training used \(\beta<1\). checks.location: Definition3.1 absorption sufficient threshold; Section3.1 SC criterion
checks.claim: This ratio condition guarantees absorption a+b=a for p=24 binary32 precision.
checks.explanation: Rounding to the nearest representable value depends on half the spacing to the adjacent value in the direction of the perturbation. Losing lower significand bits does not mean that the rounded result stays equal to the larger operand. A single exactly representable positive normal pair refutes the stated sufficient ratio.
checks.demonstration:
Under binary32 round-to-nearest, ties-to-even, choose
\[
a=1,\qquad b=3\cdot2^{-25}<2^{-23}.
\]
The next value above one is \(1+2^{-23}\), with midpoint \(1+2^{-24}\). Since \(b=\tfrac34\,2^{-23}>2^{-24}\),
\[
\operatorname{fl}(1+3\cdot2^{-25})=1+2^{-23}\ne1.
\]
Both inputs are exactly representable. For comparison, \(\operatorname{fl}(1+2^{-25})=1\); the midpoint \(b=2^{-24}\) also rounds to one because its significand is even.

For two-class shifted softmax, a margin of \(16.5>23\log2\) has residual \(\exp(-16.5)>2^{-24}\). Rounding that residual to binary32 and adding it to one produces a value greater than one. Thus even the two-class margin implication is insufficient; multiple classes additionally require control of the summed residuals.
checks.repair:
State absorption using the adjacent floating-point spacing and the rounding mode. For positive \(b\), a sufficient strict condition is
\[
b<\frac{\operatorname{nextafter}(a,+\infty)-a}{2},
\]
and for negative \(b\) use half the spacing toward \(-\infty\). Treat midpoint parity, subnormal boundaries, and overflow separately. For a single correctly rounded shifted-softmax addition with exact positive residual sum \(S\), \(S<2^{-24}\) suffices at \(a=1\). A uniform margin implies this idealized condition if \((K-1)e^{-m}<2^{-24}\). Elementary-function approximation and the actual reduction order must also be accounted for before asserting a particular fused cross-entropy kernel collapses. The existence of absorption at other inputs is not disputed.
checks.scope: The finding concerns the sufficient binary32 absorption condition and its universal softmax-margin implication. A claim about a particular kernel additionally requires its elementary-function approximation and reduction order.

checks.demonstration:
Take four states \(0,1,2,3\), initial state \(0\), one action for each player, no target states, horizon \(H=2\) and rewards equal to \(1\). Let the transition support be
\[0\to1\to2\to3,\qquad 3\to\{0,1\}.\]
Every state–action pair is reached along the deterministic initial path before the first random transition. Thus Assumption 1 holds with \(p_{\mathrm{reach}}=1\) for every support-preserving transition kernel.

Each sampled trajectory resets to state \(0\) and takes exactly two transitions. It samples rows \(0\) and \(1\) and ends at state \(2\); it never samples the outgoing transitions of rows \(2\) or \(3\). Repeating such trajectories cannot change this fact. The unobserved row at state \(3\) remains initialized to \((1/2,1/2)\), and its confidence set contains every support-preserving binary row \((p,1-p)\) with \(0<p<1\). Hence
\[\sup_{0<p<1}\|(p,1-p)-(1/2,1/2)\|_1=1.\]
Algorithm 1 therefore maintains
\[\Delta\geq\frac12R_{\max}H^2=2.\]
For \(\varepsilon=0.2\), the stopping threshold is \(\varepsilon/4=0.05\), so the algorithm never stops. The game has only one joint strategy and therefore an exact equilibrium. The obstruction is entirely in collecting information required by the stopping rule.

Choose the exploration policy to maximize robust reachability of the current unknown rows within that same horizon, and replace \(p_{\mathrm{reach}}\) by \(p_H\) in the trajectory budget. These are substantive restrictions on the games covered by the guarantee.

To verify the correction, fix a nonempty unknown set. A policy that reaches any one of its rows with probability at least \(p_H\) also reaches the union with that probability; the optimizing policy does at least as well. With \(N_t=\lceil p_H^{-1}\log(1/\delta_t)\rceil\) independent trajectories, the probability of no unknown-row sample is at most \(\delta_t\). Take \(\sum_t\delta_t\leq\delta_{\mathrm{cov}}\). At \(s\), action exit gives reward one and moves to terminal state \(t\); action wait gives reward zero and moves to \(g\). review-neurips-2026-155918.plainExplanation: A degree-two RPC with unit denominators can use \(r=\lambda/10^{-6}-(h/100)^2\), \(c=\phi\). Pixel \((0,0)\) then has longitude \(\lambda=10^{-10}h^2\), a curved height locus. Converting heights \(0,50,100\) to ENU at the equator leaves the middle point about \(1.5913\) meters off the endpoint chord after orthogonal projection. An orthogonal residual cannot be removed by any different scalar depth. The exact on-ray representation is false for admissible RPCs. Approximate depth ordering remains possible, and no implementation or reconstruction-quality defect is established.
